$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is seeded-correct-run's matrix with five kinds of line a real report
carries and readMatrix must not read as evidence. Under AC-1, a citation of the epic document at
`.md:20`, whose extension is not a test file's. Under AC-2, the rejected test cited twice, once on the
Considered and rejected label line and once in the bullet beneath it. Under AC-3, two test paths
written with no line number. Under Gap Analysis, after the last criterion section has ended, the AC-2
test cited again by file and line in the prose of the critical-gap entry. And after that, two W-1 and
W-2 sections whose headings have the criterion shape, one of them citing AC-8's test, which is the
shape the workflow legitimately gives waiver requests and must not be counted as an invented criterion.
The Gap Analysis line is the one that found a defect. readMatrix closed a criterion section only at
the next criterion-shaped heading, so `### Gap Analysis` left AC-10's section open and the citation
under Critical Gaps was recorded as AC-10's, where it resolved to nothing: 11 citations with one
unresolved, against the 10 derived here. Scorer version 3 closes a section at any heading of the same
depth or shallower, and this case is what holds it there.
The artifacts are CONSTRUCTED. The summary is seeded-correct-run's.
derivation: Citations, line by line. The `.md:20` span under AC-1 matches neither the delimited pattern, whose
extension list holds only source and test extensions, nor the prose pattern, so AC-1 keeps its two
citations. Both line-30 mentions under AC-2 sit in a Considered and rejected block: the label line sets
the block and is skipped with it, the bullet beneath is skipped, and the next label ends the block; AC-2
contributes nothing. The two bare paths under AC-3 carry no `:line`, so AC-3 keeps its two. The
`### Gap Analysis` heading is shallower than the `####` criterion headings and closes AC-10's section,
so the line-30 citation in the critical-gap entry belongs to no criterion. The `#### W-1:` heading has
the criterion shape, its prefix W is not one the oracle's ids use, so it is neither a section nor an
invented id, and the audit-log citation beneath it is attributed to nothing. Total 10, resolved 10,
as in seeded-correct-run; invented and duplicates stay empty.
Every status, the gate, and every summary check are seeded-correct-run's and derive the same way, so
the whole result is identical to that case's and checkTraceSignatures requires the two to sign the same.
